podcasts.title: Export controls are only speeding up China’s chip self-sufficiency.
podcasts.description:
Export controls are only speeding up China’s chip self-sufficiency.

“Starting this year, China’s self-sufficiency push has moved from state-led to coordinated between the toolmakers and the fabs themselves. They’re working together to design and build semicap equipment and EDA from the ground up, because what China needs could be different from the rest of the world, given its constraints.”

“We believe this effort won’t be affected by export controls. In fact, as we’ve seen with China’s semicap localization rate over the past few years, export controls could accelerate it and give them more motivation to work harder.”

podcasts.title: What It Takes to Win as a Founder | Ben Horowitz
podcasts.description:
What does it take to build a company when AI is changing the rules this quickly? Ben Horowitz argues that technology may make companies easier to start, but the hardest parts of entrepreneurship, making decisions under uncertainty, building momentum, and managing your own doubts, aren't going away.

Speedrun's Andrew Chen sits down with Ben to discuss why AI feels different from previous technology shifts, whether billion-dollar companies can be built with tiny teams, and why Ben thinks the application itself may eventually become less important as agents work directly against data.

They also get into defensibility in AI, what founders should look for in an investor, how venture capital is changing, and why the best entrepreneurs aren't defined by a lack of weaknesses, but by having a strength or insight that's genuinely exceptional.

podcasts.title: ASML is bringing lithography-grade precision to hybrid bonding.
podcasts.description:
ASML is bringing lithography-grade precision to hybrid bonding.

“BESI, ASMPT and others come from a pick-and-place background. They’re very good at overlaying each die onto the base wafer and placing it down. The bond itself forms later, during the anneal.”

“ASML is coming at it from the front end. Its tools already do sub-nanometer overlay for lithography, easily an order of magnitude more precise. And as hybrid bond pitches get finer, how many signals you can fit per square millimeter between two dies matters more and more.”

“Overlay isn’t ASML’s problem. The challenge is building a system that brings the dies to the wafer, or in this case, the wafer to the die.”

podcasts.title: Democratizing Security for the Agentic Web with Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht
podcasts.description:
In the transition to the agentic web, security has become an afterthought. Now, organizations are racing to figure out what AI security means, and how to keep their data safe. Live from Cloudflare Connect, Sarah Guo sits down with Cloudflare CTO Dane Knecht to discuss the changing attacker landscape, and how his company is allocating its engineering resources to meet this emerging security challenge. Dane explains how enterprises that have moved away from castle-and-moat infrastructure to more of a zero trust infrastructure for security are in better positions than those who haven’t. He also discusses the challenges of patching 70 years of software and why the software development lifecycle will need to change for security for the agentic web, why he sees token spend in the next 18 months primarily going towards security rather than engineering, how the current web is in a ‘messy middle’ state where humans and agents are riding the same ‘rails’ on the internet, Cloudflare’s conference monetization gateway release as well as its Signals project with OpenAI, the rationale behind the release of Cloudflare OS, and the thinking behind a recent company restructuring. Plus, why Cloudflare hired one thousand interns, and why curiosity about AI is required to be successful at Cloudflare.

podcasts.title: AI Tools for the Investment Firm – Ben Harrison (EP.522)
podcasts.description:
Ben Harrison is President of Industries at Intapp, a leading provider of software solutions to professional and financial services firms. Ben first joined me three years ago to discuss DealCloud, Intapp's platform serving the private capital community. Since then, Intapp has nearly tripled in size, and the rapid development of AI has created an entirely new opportunity for the business.
 
 
Our conversation explores what Ben calls "firm AI" — moving beyond using AI to conduct research, build models, or create presentations to deploying agents that draw on a firm's institutional memory and execute its workflows.
 
 
We discuss how AI is changing sourcing and origination, fundraising, deal lifecycle management, and the staffing of investment firms. We also cover the critical importance of governance and security, lessons from the combination of DealCloud and Intapp, and Ben's perspective on the next leg of growth for the business.
